# Shopify + Atoms: AI Voice Order Status and Returns Support

![Cinematic dark teal illustration showing an AI voice assistant connected to Shopify through secure data integration, enabling automated order tracking, shipment updates, and return request support.](https://framerusercontent.com/images/lJVbqZsOckQ3X4j62k2D03Hwko.png?width=1672&height=941)

Build a Shopify AI voice agent with Smallest.ai Atoms to check order status, handle return requests, verify customers, and hand off complex support cases.

A customer calls your store and asks, “Where is my order?” The information may already be available in Shopify's order records, fulfillment details, or the shipping carrier's tracking system. But getting that information during a support call can still take several steps. A support agent has to find the order, establish who is calling, check the latest status, and translate that record into a useful answer.

Now change the question: “Can I return the shoes from that order?” The interaction looks almost identical from the customer’s side. Behind the scenes, it is a different kind of problem. An order lookup reads data. A return request may change a workflow, create a record, and set customer expectations that the store must honor.

This is where **Shopify + Smallest.ai Atoms** becomes useful. Atoms handles the live conversation and decides when to use a configured tool. Shopify remains the source of truth for order and return records. A secure integration layer connects Atoms to Shopify, verifies customer access, and enforces which order details the agent can retrieve and which actions it can perform.

This guide walks through that architecture, shows how to configure it from the Atoms dashboard, and explains the decisions that matter before you send real customers to the agent.

## **What does the agent need to do?**

Start with a small set of tasks. Instead of trying to automate every Shopify support request, start with a few predictable tasks the agent can handle reliably. Order tracking and return eligibility are practical starting points, especially when the agent knows when to transfer a conversation to a human.

| **Customer asks** | **What the system must do** | **Safe outcome** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| “Where is my order?” | Verify the caller; read order and fulfillment data; add carrier status only when available. | Give the latest confirmed status, not an invented delivery date. |
| “Has my package shipped?” | Check each shipment or fulfillment, not just the overall order. | Explain if the order is partially fulfilled or split. |
| “Can I return this item?” | Identify the item; check applicable merchant rules and returnable items. | Explain eligibility or route an exception for review. |
| “Please start a return.” | Capture a reason, read back the choice, obtain confirmation, submit the approved workflow. | Report the request ID and its actual state, not a promised refund. |

Two requirements cut across every row: **verify access before disclosing order-specific information**, and **only describe actions that the backend confirms**. These rules are more important than a clever script.

## **The architecture at a glance**

Think of this system as a conversation layer connected to a commerce layer through a guarded doorway.

![Architecture diagram showing how Smallest.ai Atoms connects customer voice calls to Shopify order and return records through a secure, verified API bridge, with knowledge base and human handoff support.](https://framerusercontent.com/images/oi1che9KzxOU1nz3WBxofHv2E.png?width=1672&height=941)

**Supporting paths:** Atoms can consult a knowledge base for approved general policies, transfer a call to a person, and send post-call events to your reporting or support system. Shipping updates may need to come from a carrier or fulfillment service when Shopify has no recent tracking milestone.

|     |
| --- |
| **IMPORTANT DISTINCTION** As of October 2026, Shopify is **not listed as a native one-click integration** in the [documented Atoms integration catalog](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/integrate/integrations). The implementation here uses Atoms API tools connected to an authorized Shopify integration service. Do not treat a tool configuration as an automatic Shopify account connection. |

### **Why put a bridge between Atoms and Shopify?**

Because the voice agent should not be the part of your stack that decides whether an order belongs to the caller, whether a return falls inside a policy window, or whether a write can happen twice. A secure integration layer, built with an approved automation platform or a lightweight backend, can verify order ownership, enforce return policies, prevent duplicate requests, and send only the relevant results back to Atoms.

A bridge also keeps Shopify credentials out of conversational prompts. Shopify Admin API calls use authenticated store access and approved scopes. The bridge owns those credentials; the voice agent gets only the response fields it needs.

## **Workflow 1: “Where is my order?”**

Let’s follow a normal call before opening the configuration screen.

**1.  Recognize the intent.** The caller says, “I ordered a jacket last Tuesday. Has it shipped?” Atoms routes the conversation to the order-status workflow.

**2.  Capture an order reference.** Ask for an order number. Repeat ambiguous letters or digits rather than guessing from noisy audio.

**3.  Verify the caller.** The integration verifies the caller using the store's approved authentication process, such as a one-time code delivered through a trusted channel and validated by the backend. The agent proceeds only after verification succeeds. An order number or caller ID alone should not be treated as proof of ownership.

**4.  Fetch the authorized order.** Once verified, the backend retrieves the matching order and its fulfillment details from Shopify. If the order contains two shipments, keep those shipments separate.

**5.  Translate structured fields into speech.** “Your jacket was fulfilled yesterday. The carrier has not published a delivery estimate yet.” This gives the customer a useful update without confusing order fulfillment with confirmed delivery.

**6.  Offer a useful next action.** If the customer needs the tracking link, use an approved messaging flow or guide them to the order page. If the data is inconsistent, offer human support.

The underlying response should distinguish order state, fulfillment state, tracking availability, and the timestamp of the last confirmed update. “Fulfilled” is not the same as “delivered,” and “label created” is not the same as “collected by carrier.”

## **Workflow 2: “I want to return this item”**

Returns need a separate workflow because the agent may need to do more than retrieve information. It may also need to check eligibility, collect customer details, and submit a request that changes the store's records. Shopify supports merchant-defined return windows, final-sale exclusions, fees, and other conditions. Those rules may differ by product or market, and updates to return rules do not automatically rewrite the rules that applied to earlier purchases. See [Shopify’s return-rule guidance](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/managing-orders/returns/return-rules).

![Five-step Shopify AI voice return workflow showing customer verification, return eligibility checks, customer confirmation, secure API request submission, and a pending return request awaiting merchant review, not an automatic refund.](https://framerusercontent.com/images/qQWAIyJ8NcSBM9xcXVEwHqEJDbA.png?width=1672&height=941)

**1.  Find and verify the order.** Reuse the verified order context from the earlier step, or verify the caller if this is a new call.

**2.  Identify the exact item and quantity.** A customer might have purchased two sizes or received the same item in separate fulfillments. Never infer which unit they mean.

**3.  Check returnability and store policy.** The backend checks the order's applicable return policy and queries Shopify's returnable fulfillment data to identify eligible items and quantities. It also checks for existing returns or other restrictions before the agent explains the available options.

**4.  Ask for the reason.** Capture the reason required by the merchant’s workflow, including any notes that need to travel with the request.

**5.  Confirm before writing.** “You’d like to request a return for one blue shirt from order 1042 because the size is too small. Should I submit that request?”

**6.  Submit the correct operation.** For merchant review, Shopify documents returnRequest, which creates a return in REQUESTED state. returnCreate instead creates an OPEN return and assumes approval has already occurred. These are not interchangeable. See [Shopify’s return-management guide](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/orders-fulfillment/returns-apps/build-return-management).

**7.  Read back the confirmed result.** Say 'Your return request has been submitted for review' only after the backend confirms that Shopify created the return request, returned its reference and REQUESTED status, and reported no mutation errors. If the result is uncertain, explain that the request could not be confirmed and offer further assistance. Give the actual reference and next step. Do not promise a label, approval, or refund that the backend has not confirmed.

![Dark teal illustration of a Shopify AI voice return workflow showing customer verification, item selection, return eligibility checks, reason collection, customer confirmation, and return request submission for merchant review.](https://framerusercontent.com/images/tzUHWc5SIvFavGO4upTKFBg8cSo.png?width=1672&height=941)

## **How to build Shopify + Atoms without a large codebase**

A practical starting architecture uses the Atoms dashboard to configure conversations and API tools, with a separate secure integration layer handling Shopify authentication, customer verification, and return-policy checks. Depending on your existing tools, you can configure this integration through an approved low-code automation platform or build a lightweight backend for greater control. The example endpoint names below are **illustrative**, not native Shopify or Atoms endpoints.

![Four-step illustration showing how to build a Shopify AI voice support agent with Smallest.ai Atoms: configure Shopify API access, establish a secure integration bridge, set up Atoms tools, and test the voice workflow before activation. ](https://framerusercontent.com/images/OmV31UQm6viyQGYVRMhpRaYMCE0.png?width=1672&height=941)

### **Step 1. Prepare Shopify data and permissions**

In your Shopify admin, review **Settings → Policies** and confirm your return and cancellation rules, including the window, final-sale exclusions, fees, and product exceptions. Write down which requests the agent can handle and which need a human decision.

For data access, use an authorized Shopify app and the current GraphQL Admin API authentication model. New app work follows Shopify’s Dev Dashboard or CLI process, not the discontinued flow for creating a new admin-created custom app. Ask for the minimum permitted scopes. Order lookups generally require the `read_orders` scope. Reading return records or returnable fulfillments also requires appropriate return access, such as `read_returns`, while submitting return requests requires `write_returns`. Access to orders older than 60 days generally requires additional Shopify approval and the `read_all_orders` scope.

Store Shopify credentials securely in the integration service and never expose them in agent prompts, customer-visible variables, or public endpoints. Handle token acquisition and renewal according to the authentication method used, including token expiration where applicable.

### **Step 2. Expose a small set of safe actions**

Your integration service should do the hard work: verify ownership, query Shopify, apply store policy, and normalize responses. From Atoms, the workflow then looks like four business actions instead of many raw commerce API calls.

| **Illustrative action** | **Input from Atoms** | **Response the agent needs** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| verify\_order | Order reference plus the required verification inputs. | A server-issued verification reference, or a safe failure result. |
| get\_order\_status | Verified reference. | Order state, line/shipment status, tracking summary, last updated timestamp. |
| check\_return\_eligibility | Verified reference, selected item and quantity. | Eligible / not eligible / human review; allowed next step; policy reason. |
| submit\_return\_request | Verified reference, item, quantity, reason, explicit customer confirmation. | Request reference and actual state, or a clear error. |

Use short error codes such as verification\_failed, order\_not\_found, tracking\_unavailable, human\_review\_required, and request\_already\_exists. The agent can map these to plain speech without exposing internal diagnostics. For return submissions, assign a stable idempotency key to each customer-confirmed request and enforce it in the backend. If a call times out or the agent retries, the backend should reuse that key, check whether a return already exists, and avoid submitting the same request twice.

### **Step 3. Create the customer-support agent in Atoms**

Sign in to the [Smallest.ai console](https://app.smallest.ai/login?entry=root) and create a new voice agent for Shopify customer support. In the editor, set a support-focused name, the primary spoken language, a voice, and a prompt describing exactly which tasks are in scope. Atoms documents the dashboard setup and its separate **Publish** and **Activate** steps in the [agent setup guide](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/build-your-agent).

Keep the first version narrow: order lookups, return eligibility, return request submission, and transfer. Leave address edits, cancellations, payments, and refunds outside the pilot unless you have built and approved those flows independently.

### **Step 4. Add the return-policy knowledge base**

Create a knowledge base containing your current written return policy, shipping FAQs, contact hours, and escalation conditions. Upload an approved policy document or use the supported Extract from URL option to import website content. Once the documents have finished processing, enable Knowledge Base in the agent configuration and select the relevant knowledge base. Atoms documents this under [Knowledge Base](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/knowledge-base).

This is where general questions belong: “How long do I have to return something?” Order-specific questions still need verified live data. Review the knowledge base whenever policies change.

### **Step 5. Configure the API tools in Atoms**

In the **Tools** library, choose **Add tool → API tool**. Name the action, explain when the agent should use it, and configure the HTTP method and secure bridge URL. Atoms provides Path, Params, Headers, Auth, and Body settings, along with variable mapping and response extraction. The inline Test API feature can test requests, but it does not inject saved authentication secrets. Authenticated endpoints may therefore return a 401 or 403 response during inline testing and should also be verified through an actual agent call. See the [API tool guide](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/tools/api-tool).

For example, configure get\_order\_status to call the bridge’s authenticated order-status endpoint. Map the verification reference from a variable populated by the successful verification workflow. The backend must validate this reference instead of trusting an unverified value supplied by the caller or generated by the model. Store the bridge API credential in [Atoms Secrets](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/tools/secrets) and reference it from the Auth tab.

| **Tool setting** | **Example configuration** | **Why it matters** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | get\_order\_status | The model can select a specific action. |
| Method / URL | GET / https://support.example.com/orders/status | Calls your bridge, not an open Shopify token endpoint. |
| Parameter | verification\_ref ← verified variable | Passes the verified reference to the backend, which must independently validate its authenticity, validity period, and authorization before returning order information. |
| Authentication | Bearer secret ORDER\_BRIDGE\_TOKEN | Credential is injected server-side. |
| Response extraction | status ← $.status, tracking ← $.tracking\_summary | Keeps spoken replies grounded in returned fields. |
| Test | Valid, invalid, expired, and unavailable cases | Checks request structure and response handling. Verify authenticated requests and complete error-handling behavior through Test Agent and backend tests. |

Then attach these saved tools to the agent in its **Tools** tab. Atoms reusable tools are shared across agents, so editing a library tool can affect every agent referencing it. Duplicate the library tool and give the test copy its own configuration and identifier when you need isolated testing without affecting agents that use the original tool. See [Tools library](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/tools/tools-library).

### **Step 6. Tell the agent when to use each tool**

A connected tool is not the same as a reliable workflow. Your prompt needs to say when the tool should run and what counts as a completed action. Here is a compact starting instruction to adapt in the agent editor:

|     |
| --- |
| **EXAMPLE AGENT INSTRUCTION**“You are the Shopify store’s order and returns assistant. For order-specific questions, request the order reference and complete the required verification tool first. Do not reveal customer or shipment details before verification. Use get\_order\_status only with a verified reference. For returns, confirm the item and quantity, call check\_return\_eligibility, and ask the caller for explicit approval before submit\_return\_request. State only statuses and references returned by tools. Never say a refund is issued unless an authorized system confirms that. When verification, policy checks, or tools fail, explain the limitation and offer a human transfer.” |

Add short voice-specific rules: ask one question at a time, read back uncertain order numbers, allow callers to interrupt or correct details, and avoid reading long tracking URLs aloud. Keep the agent from inventing delivery dates or exceptions to store policy.

### **Step 7. Add human transfer and test the complete path**

Enable Atoms’ **Transfer Call** system tool with a valid destination, and decide whether warm transfer makes sense for your support team. The documented tool can pass a short whisper message to the receiving agent in a warm transfer. Keep private details out of the message unless the transfer destination is trusted and authorized. See [system tools](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/tools/agent-tools-tab).

Use **Test Agent** with web or phone testing. Start with a browser-based Test Agent conversation and verify that the agent follows the correct workflow. Next, confirm that authenticated API requests succeed, test invalid and expired verification references, and repeat the complete process through the phone channel. When the draft is ready, publish and activate it. Use the agent’s supported phone deployment or voice widget for your chosen customer channel; adding a Shopify API connection does not automatically add a widget to your storefront.

## **No-code or low-code: which approach should you choose?**

| **Approach** | **What you configure** | **Good fit / tradeoff** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI-led, managed automation | Atoms agent and tools + approved integration workflow with Shopify authentication and simple policies. | Useful for quickly testing a low-code integration, provided the platform supports secure authentication, verification checks, Shopify API access, and reliable error handling. Complex policy rules may still require a custom backend. |
| Small custom integration service | Atoms agent and tools + a small authenticated API layer calling Shopify GraphQL. | More engineering effort, better control over verification, scope, idempotency, error handling, and audit trails. |

For either route, the agent should see a simple business response, not a raw Shopify GraphQL payload. That separation makes prompt behavior easier to test and reduces the chance of leaking sensitive fields into a spoken answer.

## **What usually breaks in production?**

An early demo may work perfectly with a single order, one shipment, and a customer who provides every detail correctly. Real stores have partial fulfillments, returns already in progress, carrier delays, and customers who say “no, the other blue shirt.” Plan for the failures now.

![Troubleshooting decision map for a Shopify AI voice-support workflow with three rows: identity verification leading to either “Read order” or “Retry or transfer,” tracking status leading to either “Share latest update” or “Give last milestone,” and return-write confirmation leading to either “State actual result” or “Reconcile first.” ](https://framerusercontent.com/images/NCpjrU8kSEHVbJ7nz4GXvk2xPQ.png?width=1672&height=941)

| **Failure mode** | **What the agent should do** |
| --- | --- |
| Order number misheard or duplicated | Repeat the ambiguous segment and recheck. Never guess a match. |
| Verification fails | Do not reveal the order. Offer retry under policy or secure human support. |
| Split shipment or partial fulfillment | Describe each item or shipment separately; avoid saying the full order was delivered. |
| Tracking feed is stale | State the last known milestone and its timestamp. Do not invent an ETA. |
| Return policy exception | Explain that manual review is required. Do not silently override store rules. |
| Request times out after submission | Check for an existing request before retrying, using the idempotency reference. |
| Customer asks for immediate refund | Explain that request, approval, receiving items, and refund processing may be separate stages. |

When something goes wrong, the agent should explain the limitation clearly rather than guess or continue with unverified information. If your integration is down, say that the order system cannot be reached. Do not continue with an answer generated from memory.

## **How do you know the workflow actually worked?**

Do not count a successful-sounding conversation as a successful Shopify action. Reconcile what the agent said with what was saved in the system.

![Split-panel illustration comparing an AI voice agent falsely confirming a Shopify return with an unverified backend record versus a verified return request showing "REQUESTED" status and a confirmed reference number, awaiting merchant review. ](https://framerusercontent.com/images/EeWXcoh0w1hKDccy2PLHTuWljg.png?width=1672&height=941)

| **Test case** | **Pass condition** |
| --- | --- |
| Valid order, correct verification | Agent announces the same fulfillment state returned by the authorized endpoint. |
| Wrong verification inputs | No private order fields are spoken or returned to the agent. |
| Two shipments, different states | Agent distinguishes both shipments rather than collapsing into one status. |
| Eligible return needing approval | The backend confirms exactly one return request in REQUESTED state, or one equivalent approved merchant workflow record, with the expected item, quantity, and reference. No mutation errors or duplicate submissions occur. |
| Tool timeout after return submission | No duplicate request is created; ambiguous outcome is escalated or reconciled. |
| Ineligible or already-refunded item | No return write occurs; caller gets the correct next step. |

Then track a small set of operational metrics: verified lookup success rate, correct order-status answer rate, return-request confirmation rate, duplicate-write incidents, tool error rate, and human-transfer rate by reason. Review a sample of calls for policy accuracy, not just conversational smoothness.

Atoms supports call transcripts, metrics, and lifecycle webhooks. Its documented event types include pre-conversation, post-conversation, and analytics-completed. These can help connect a conversation to a support ticket or audit record, but the integration should still reconcile any claimed order action against Shopify or your system of record. See [Atoms webhooks](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/integrate/webhooks).

## **Security and customer trust are part of the workflow**

An order status response can expose addresses, purchases, and other personal information. Build verification into the backend, enforce least-privilege Shopify access, and return only fields necessary for the spoken task. A caller’s phone number is a useful signal, not sufficient authentication on its own.

For return submissions, require a clear customer confirmation, write an audit record, and use an idempotent operation. Keep data retention, recording notices, consent, and access controls aligned with your store’s policies and applicable law. When you cannot verify identity or apply a policy confidently, route the customer to an authorized support person.

## **Make the conversation useful, not just fluent**

The goal is not to make a voice agent sound as if it knows every answer. It is to make a common customer problem easier to resolve without taking shortcuts around the store’s rules. Shopify should remain authoritative for orders and returns; Atoms should make those facts accessible in a natural conversation; and the integration layer should enforce what happens between them.

Begin with a verified order-status workflow that retrieves accurate Shopify data, explains the result naturally, and offers human support when necessary. Then add return requests once the state transitions are clear. [Start building with Smallest.ai Atoms](https://app.smallest.ai/) and use the [Atoms agent documentation](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/build-your-agent) to configure your first Shopify support workflow.
